arxiv-2202-07860.title: Direct Estimate of the Post-Newtonian Parameter and Cosmic Curvature from Galaxy-scale Strong Gravitational Lensing
arxiv-2202-07860.creator: Jun-Jie Wei, Yun Chen, Shuo Cao, Xue-Feng Wu
arxiv-2202-07860.description: Abstract Einstein’s theory of general relativity (GR) has been precisely tested on solar system scales, but extragalactic tests are still poorly performed. In this work, we use a newly compiled sample of galaxy-scale strong gravitational lenses to test the validity of GR on kiloparsec scales.

arxiv-2203-12540.title: String order melting of spin-1 particle chains in superconducting transmons using optimal control
arxiv-2203-12540.creator: Paul Kairys, Travis S. Humble
arxiv-2203-12540.description: Abstract Utilizing optimal control to simulate a model Hamiltonian is an emerging strategy that leverages the intrinsic physics of a device with digital quantum simulation methods. Here we evaluate optimal control for probing the non-equilibrium properties of symmetry-protected topological (SPT) states simulated with superconducting hardware.

arxiv-2308-14878.title: Dominance of extrinsic scattering mechanisms in the orbital Hall effect: graphene, transition metal dichalcogenides and topological antiferromagnets
arxiv-2308-14878.creator: Hong Liu, Dimitrie Culcer
arxiv-2308-14878.description: Abstract The theory of the orbital Hall effect (OHE), a transverse flow of orbital angular momentum (OAM) in response to an electric field, has concentrated on intrinsic mechanisms. Here, using a quantum kinetic formulation, we determine the full OHE in the presence of short-range disorder using 2D massive Dirac fermions as a prototype.

arxiv-2412-00622.title: Visual Mod ality Prompt for Adapting Vision-Language Object Detectors
arxiv-2412-00622.creator: Heitor R. Medeiros .Atif BelalSrikanth MuralidharanEric GrangerMarco PedersoliLIVIA, Dept. of Systems Engineering, ETS Montreal, CanadaInternational Laboratory on Learning Systems (ILLS)
arxiv-2412-00622.description: Abstract The zero-shot performance of object detectors degrades when tested on different modalities, such as infrared and depth. While recent work has explored image translation techniques to adapt detectors to new modalities, these methods are limited to a single modality and apply only to traditional detectors.

arxiv-2412-19866.title: Asymptotic expansions for the reciprocal Hardy-Littlewood logarithmic integrals Thanks: Email: glenn.bruda@ufl.edu
arxiv-2412-19866.creator: Glenn Bruda
arxiv-2412-19866.description: Abstract . Defining a family of recurrences, we generalize Comtet’s formula for the generating function of the enumeration of indecomposable permutations. Consequently, we generalize Panaitopol’s asymptotic expansion for the prime counting function, obtaining asymptotic expansions salient to the first Hardy-Littlewood conjecture. 1. Introduction Preliminarily, a permutation \sigma of length n\in\mathbb{Z}^{+} is a bijection \sigma:\{1,2,\dots,n\}\to\{1,2,\dots,n\} .

arxiv-2503-22621.title: Improved error estimates for low-regularity integrators using space-time bounds Thanks: Funded by the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG, German Research Foundation) – Project-ID 258734477 – SFB 1173. Thanks: I thank Benjamin Dörich and Roland Schnaubelt for fruitful discussions. I also thank the
arxiv-2503-22621.creator: Maximilian Ruff
arxiv-2503-22621.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Maximilian Ruff. We prove optimal convergence rates for certain low-regularity integrators applied to the one-dimensional periodic nonlinear Schrödinger and wave equations under the assumption of H 1 H^{1} solutions. For the Schrödinger equation we analyze the exponential-type scheme proposed by Ostermann and Schratz in 2018, whereas in the wave case we treat the corrected Lie splitting proposed by Li, Schratz, and Zivcovich in 2023. We show that the integrators converge with their full order of one and two, respectively.

arxiv-2504-07384.title: Convergence-divergence models: Generalizations of phylogenetic trees modeling gene flow over time
arxiv-2504-07384.creator: Jonathan D.Mitchell, Barbara R.Holland
arxiv-2504-07384.description: Abstract Phylogenetic trees are simple models of evolutionary processes. They describe conditionally independent divergent evolution of taxa from common ancestors. Phylogenetic trees commonly do not have enough flexibility to adequately model all evolutionary processes. For example, introgressive hybridization, where genes can flow from one taxon to another. Phylogenetic networks model evolution not fully described by a phylogenetic tree.

arxiv-2505-09790.title: ValveFit : An analysis-suitable B-spline-based surface fitting framework for patient-specific modeling of tricuspid valves
arxiv-2505-09790.creator: Ajith Moola, Ashton M. Corpuz, Michael J. Burkhart, Colton J. Ross, Arshid Mir, Harold M. Burkhart, Chung-Hao Lee, Ming-Chen Hsu, Aishwarya Pawar
arxiv-2505-09790.description: Abstract Patient-specific computational modeling of the tricuspid valve (TV) is vital for the clinical assessment of heart valve diseases. However, this process is hindered by limitations inherent in the medical image data, such as noise and sparsity, as well as by complex valve dynamics.

arxiv-2508-17693.title: Database Normalization via Dual-LLM Self-Refinement CCS: Information systems Relational database model CCS: Computing methodologies Reasoning about belief and knowledge
arxiv-2508-17693.creator: Eunjae Jo, Nakyung Lee, and Gyuyeong Kim
arxiv-2508-17693.description: Abstract . Database normalization is crucial to preserving data integrity. However, it is time-consuming and error-prone, as it is typically performed manually by data engineers. To this end, we present Miffie, a database normalization framework that leverages the capability of large language models. Miffie enables automated data normalization without human effort while preserving high accuracy.

arxiv-2509-23152.title: Critique to Verify: Accurate and Honest Test-Time Scaling with RL-Trained Verifiers
arxiv-2509-23152.creator: Zhicheng Yang Zhijiang Guo Yinya Huang Yongxin Wang, Yiwei Wang Xiaodan Liang Jing Tang, The Hong Kong University of Science, Technology (Guangzhou), The Hong Kong University of Science, Technology ETH AI Center, ETH Zurich, University of California, Merced Sun Yat-sen University MBZUAI yangzhch6@gm
arxiv-2509-23152.description: Abstract Test-time scaling via solution sampling and aggregation has become a key paradigm for improving the reasoning performance of Large Language Models (LLMs). While reward model selection is commonly employed in this approach, it often fails to identify minority-yet-correct answers, which limits its effectiveness beyond that of simple majority voting.

pmc-10539570.title: Expression And Prognostic Role of PRDX1 In Gastrointestinal Cancers
pmc-10539570.creator: Zhou Zhang, Pengli Zhou, Mingyue Liu, Bing Pei
pmc-10539570.description: Esophageal, gastric, liver, and colorectal cancers represent four prevalent gastrointestinal cancers that pose substantial threats to global health due to their high morbidity and mortality rates. Peroxiredoxin 1 (PRDX1), a significant component of the PRDXs family, primarily functions to counteract the peroxides produced by metabolic activities in the body, thereby maintaining the dynamic equilibrium of peroxides in vivo.

pmc-10574168.title: Alterations in Placental Inflammation-Related Gene Expression Partially Mediate the Effects of Prenatal Alcohol Consumption on Maternal Iron Homeostasis
pmc-10574168.creator: Jacqueline J Masehi-Lano, Maya Deyssenroth, Sandra W Jacobson, Joseph L Jacobson, Christopher D Molteno, Neil C Dodge, Helen C Wainwright, Ernesta M Meintjes, Corina Lesseur, Haoxiang Cheng, Qian Li, Ke Hao, Jia Chen, R Colin Carter, Fudi Wang
pmc-10574168.description: Prenatal alcohol exposure (PAE) is associated with alterations in maternal and infant iron homeostasis that are consistent with changes seen in the setting of inflammation. We hypothesized that PAE leads to alterations in the placental expression of genes related to iron metabolism and inflammation that play functional roles in the teratogenic effects of alcohol on iron homeostasis.

pmc-10618840.title: Virtual Reality–Based Intervention to Reduce Preoperative Anxiety in Adults Undergoing Elective Surgery
pmc-10618840.creator: Pak Lung Chiu, Huiyuan Li, Kevin Yi-Lwern Yap, Ka-man Carmen Lam, Pui-ling Renee Yip, Cho Lee Wong
pmc-10618840.description: Key PointsQuestionCompared with standard care, can a virtual reality–based intervention with preoperative education improve preoperative anxiety in adult patients undergoing elective surgery?FindingsThis randomized clinical trial of 74 adult patients undergoing elective surgery found that a virtual reality–based intervention was effective in reducing preoperative anxiety.

pmc-10629448.title: Mothers’ Attitudes Towards Breastfeeding in Terms of Health Safety and Professional Lactation Education: A National Survey of Women
pmc-10629448.creator: Anna Bednarek, Iwona Bodys-Cupak, Adrianna Serwin, Elżbieta Cipora
pmc-10629448.description: Introduction and ObjectiveAn important role in building opinions and attitudes regarding breastfeeding by mothers is played by the medical staff taking care of the mother woman expecting a baby. Breastfeeding is a standard in infant nutrition. The knowledge and support of the medical staff can help a woman make the decision to breastfeed.

pmc-13462905.title: Prediction of Antimicrobial Resistance in People Living With Cystic Fibrosis Using Machine Learning
pmc-13462905.creator: Junrong Jiang, Akhil Naik, Dilip Nazareth, Dennis Wat, Graham Hyde, Jo Fothergill, Sarah Benabidallah, Gregory Y. H. Lip, Sandra Ortega‐Martorell, Ivan Olier, Freddy Frost
pmc-13462905.description: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a growing challenge in people living with cystic fibrosis (pwCF), who often experience chronic lung infection and repeated antibiotic exposure. Because routine antibiotic susceptibility testing often takes several days, treatment is frequently started before current resistance profiles are available.

pmc-13623254.creator: Seshan Kumar, Abdul Qadir Jilani, Saloni Singh
pmc-13623254.description: usation.[2] Quetiapine is a second-generation antipsychotic with predominant 5-HT2A antagonism and an active metabolite, norquetiapine, that enhances antidepressant effects via norepinephrine reuptake inhibition.[3] Despite its favorable tolerability profile, quetiapine-induced cutaneous adverse reactions are rarely reported.[4] We present a case of quetiapine-induced acneiform eruption in a patient with bipolar depression.

uslaw-usc-t36-s23107.title: 36 U.S.C. § 23107 — Principal office
uslaw-usc-t36-s23107.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t36-s23107.description: United States Code, Title 36 (Patriotic And National Observances, Ceremonies, And Organizations); Part B (Organizations); Chapter 231 (Aviation Hall Of Fame). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The principal office of the corporation shall be in Ohio. However, the activities of the corporation are not confined to the place where the principal office is located but may be conducted throughout the States, territories.

uslaw-usc-t50-s3820.title: 50 U.S.C. § 3820 — Procedural rights
uslaw-usc-t50-s3820.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t50-s3820.description: United States Code, Title 50 (War And National Defense); Chapter 49 (Military Selective Service). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) It is hereby declared to be the purpose of this section to guarantee to each registrant asserting a claim before a local or appeal board, a fair hearing consistent with the informal and expeditious processing which is required by selective service cases.
